LOOK_AT.say: The storekeeper, behind his counter, in sleeve garters, with a pencil behind each ear.
repeat: He keeps one hand on the ledger at all times, the way other men keep a hand on a gun.
He smiles at everyone who comes in. He has a page for every one of them.
Still adding. He has not yet subtracted anything.
Nothing. He's stopped writing to watch what I'm holding.

exchange.speaker: storekeeper
exchange.line: Whatever a man needs to find gold. Picks, pans, maps, peaches.

exchange.speaker: storekeeper
exchange.line: Not yet. That's why they keep needing it.

exchange.speaker: storekeeper
exchange.line: You have one. I opened it when the coach came in. Everybody's got one.

exchange.speaker: thad
exchange.line: And if a man can't pay?

exchange.speaker: storekeeper
exchange.line: Then he stays. I've never lost a customer.

options.text: Is that dynamite next to the stove?

exchange.speaker: storekeeper
exchange.line: Dry and warm. It's never been happier.

options.text: Your scales lean to one side.
options.say: Toward me. Everything in here does, eventually.

exchange.speaker: storekeeper
exchange.line: Ruled off. The undertaker has the rest of him.

options.say: I ruled him off. I don't rule off the living. It's bad for business.
Look all you like. It's free until you touch something.
